logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, pinning keeps a notification available separately from its read status. If an already-read notification is pinned, its row actions and the unread count change as though it became unread, unexpectedly altering the state of a message that had already been read.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Read/unread and pinned are mutually exclusive NotificationStatus enum values. Pinning changes Read to Pinned; templates render pinned rows with unread-style Mark as read controls rather than retaining an independent read flag.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, pinning keeps a notification available separately from its read status. If an already-read notification is pinned, its row actions and the unread count change as though it became unread, unexpectedly altering the state of a message that had already been read.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, notifications > Subscriptions lists work items the user follows. At narrow phone width, its toolbar clips the Sort control and the opened sort menu extends past the right edge, leaving option labels unreadable or unreachable instead of fitting the screen.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The subscriptions template places state/type/sort controls in horizontal flex/filter menus without a narrow-width wrapping rule or viewport-constrained dropdown. The toolbar intrinsic width clips Sort, and opening that clipped menu leaves its labels offscreen.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, notifications > Subscriptions lists work items the user follows. At narrow phone width, its toolbar clips the Sort control and the opened sort menu extends past the right edge, leaving option labels unreadable or unreachable instead of fitting the screen.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, notifications > Watching lists repositories the user follows. Choosing Smallest size or Largest size changes the address to that sort, but the rows and active sort indicator stay on Recently updated, so the size choice never takes effect.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NotificationWatching has no size/reversesize switch cases. Those query values fall through to recentupdate, overwriting SortType and using recent updated ordering; both the rows and highlighted menu entry are therefore wrong.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, notifications > Watching lists repositories the user follows. Choosing Smallest size or Largest size changes the address to that sort, but the rows and active sort indicator stay on Recently updated, so the size choice never takes effect.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, alphabetical repository ordering is case-sensitive in profile Repositories and Notifications > Watching. A name beginning with an uppercase letter can appear ahead of lowercase names that should precede it alphabetically, rather than treating capitalization consistently for a human-readable name sort.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SearchOrderByAlphabetically orders name ASC rather than lower_name or a case-insensitive expression. The SQLite fixture therefore orders uppercase names ahead of lowercase names across repository lists.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea profile’s Repositories list or Notifications > Watching, choose alphabetical repository ordering with a mixture of uppercase and lowercase names. An uppercase name can sort before lowercase names that precede it alphabetically, instead of ignoring case for the name ordering.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Notifications with the Read view selected, use a row action such as Pin or Mark as unread. The redirect drops the Read filter and opens the default Unread view, unexpectedly abandoning the list the user was managing.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NotificationStatusPost redirects with page only and getNotifications chooses Read solely from q=read. Status forms do not retain q, so a read-view action returns to the default Unread view.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Notifications with the Read view selected, use a row action such as Pin or Mark as unread. The redirect drops the Read filter and opens the default Unread view, unexpectedly abandoning the list the user was managing.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea issue (a tracked work item) page, clicking the repository's Unwatch button updates only the header. The issue sidebar's Notifications button, which inherits the repository watch, keeps showing Unsubscribe until the page is reloaded, and clicking it sends the stale action.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The repository watch/unwatch form uses htmx hx-target="this", replacing only that header form. The issue subscription form separately renders its hidden watch value and button label from IssueWatch.IsWatching and is not a target of the repository response, so its inherited state remains stale until reload.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea issue page, clicking the repository's Unwatch button updates only the header. The issue sidebar's Notifications button, which inherits the repository watch, keeps showing Unsubscribe until the page is reloaded, and clicking it sends the stale action.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with a page open, new notifications (a mention, or new issues (tracked work items) in a watched repository) never update the bell's unread count or the open Notifications list. The new count and notifications appear only after a reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SharedWorker sends {type,data}, where data is the SSE JSON string. The message handler passes the outer MessageEvent to receiveUpdateCount, which JSON.parse(event.data) attempts to parse the envelope object. It throws before updating count/table; the successful worker branch also returns without starting the periodic fallback.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with a page open, new notifications (a mention, or new issues in a watched repository) never update the bell's unread count or the open Notifications list. The new count and notifications appear only after a reload.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, pinned notifications consume slots in the same paginated Read or Unread list as ordinary rows, but the page count excludes those pinned rows. With enough notifications, ordinary rows disappear beyond the last available page even though they still exist.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getNotifications counts only the requested read/unread status but selects rows with both that status and Pinned using the same page size. The undercount hides a next page even when pinned rows displace ordinary rows.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Notifications > Unread, pinned messages share page slots with unread rows but are not included in the pagination total. Enough pinned messages push ordinary unread notifications beyond the last reachable page instead of keeping all messages accessible.

On Gitea’s Notifications > Read, pinned messages occupy slots in the same list without being included in its page count. Some ordinary read notifications therefore fall beyond the final available page even though they still exist.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a user is removed as a collaborator from a private repository, their Notifications list still shows notifications from it, including the private repository's name and the issue's title. Opening one leads to a 404, and the entry stays listed. The list loads repositories and issues (tracked work items) without checking whether the user can still read them.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getNotifications loads repositories/issues by ID and removes only missing records. It does not check current actor read permission after access is revoked, so stored private notification metadata remains visible.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a user is removed as a collaborator from a private repository, their Notifications list still shows notifications from it, including the private repository's name and the issue's title. Opening one leads to a 404, and the entry stays listed. The list loads repositories and issues without checking whether the user can still read them.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a user is removed from a private repository, new activity on an issue (a tracked work item) they were subscribed to still shows up in their Notifications: the issue's entry jumps back to the top as 'now' each time someone comments, telling them there is new private activity they can no longer open.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Source attribution remains unresolved: retained issue watches/participant rows supply candidate recipients, but the pinned createOrUpdateIssueNotifications implementation explicitly checks CheckRepoUnitUser before updating an existing notification. The reported continued updates cannot be attributed to an absent permission check in this revision; a distinct deployment revision, permission state or delivery path must be established before merging this with the display-only permission defect. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a user is removed from a private repository, new activity on an issue they were subscribed to still shows up in their Notifications: the issue's entry jumps back to the top as 'now' each time someone comments, telling them there is new private activity they can no longer open.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Notifications > Watching, unwatching the only repository on the last page and coming back to that page shows "No matching results found." with no pagination, even though earlier pages still list watched repositories. Unlike Subscriptions, the Watching page never redirects an out-of-range page to the last valid one.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NotificationWatching creates pagination after querying the requested page but never compares its clamped current page with the request or redirects. An empty out-of-range result therefore has no usable page controls despite earlier records.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Notifications > Watching, unwatching the only repository on the last page and coming back to that page shows "No matching results found." with no pagination, even though earlier pages still list watched repositories. Unlike Subscriptions, the Watching page never redirects an out-of-range page to the last valid one.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a user reads an issue (a tracked work item) notification and pins it, a new comment on the issue moves the pinned notification to the top with a new time, but opening it still scrolls to and highlights the earlier comment the user already read instead of the new comment.
logicalBugs.rootCause: updateIssueNotification changes CommentID only when the previous status is Read. A pinned notification follows the else branch, updating activity/order metadata while retaining its old comment link.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a user reads an issue notification and pins it, a new comment on the issue moves the pinned notification to the top with a new time, but opening it still scrolls to and highlights the earlier comment the user already read instead of the new comment.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s Subscriptions page should list issues the user follows through direct subscription, participation or watching their repository. Instead, it can include an issue from a repository the user never watched or has unwatched, even though that issue’s sidebar offers Subscribe and its subscription check is false. It can also omit issues from watched repositories. The incorrect results persist independently of the sidebar’s separate stale-button issue and depend on how database record IDs happen to line up.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Subscriptions query’s watched-repository condition compares issue.repo_id with SELECT id FROM watch instead of SELECT repo_id FROM watch. A watch record’s own identifier is not its repository identifier, so accidental numeric matches include unrelated repositories while nonmatching IDs omit watched ones. Direct subscription checks and notification delivery use repo_id correctly, explaining their disagreement with the list.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, open Subscriptions after another user creates an issue in a repository you never watched, or after you unwatch its repository. The issue can appear there while its sidebar offers Subscribe and its subscription check is false, with no notification. Whether it appears depends on watch-row and repository ID collisions, so one correctly behaving repository is not a sufficient negative control.

In Gitea, watch a repository and confirm that an issue there is effectively subscribed through that watch. The issue can be missing from Subscriptions when the watch row’s own ID differs from the repository ID, even though the subscription check and notification behavior recognize the repository watch.
